#Wren licences

Wren is a beta under development and every version is free. A supporter licence only supports its development: it unlocks nothing, nothing in Wren checks it, and no window or reminder asks for one. The only visible effect is one line of about:wren:

  • without a licence: Unregistered — free during the beta · Support Wren;
  • with one: Registered to <name>, with the edition, the date, the order number and a thank-you.

The code is under the PolyForm Strict License 1.0.0 (LICENSE). A supporter licence is separate from the code's license.

#How it works

A licence is a statement signed offline with an Ed25519 private key that only the maintainer has. Wren holds the matching public key and checks the signature on the user's computer, without any network access (core:crypto/ed25519, package src/license). No server is involved in checking. Issuing is either manual (the maintainer signs a licence with tools\license.ps1 and sends it) or automatic: licences are sold through Paddle (the seller of record, who handles VAT), and a small Cloudflare Worker (licence/worker, free plan) signs the licence when Paddle reports a paid transaction, keeps it, mails it, and shows it on the thank-you page. Both produce byte-identical licences; see Selling with Paddle.

(The folder is licence, not license: on Windows license would collide with the LICENSE file at the root.)

#Format

The text of a licence (what is pasted in about:wren, or kept in a .wrenlicense file):

WREN1.<payload>.<signature>
  • payload: base64url (no padding) of a JSON object {"product":"wren","edition":"supporter","name":"…","email":"…","date":"2026-10-22","order":"WREN-0001"}. edition is supporter or patron (the same licence, a stronger support); unknown fields and unknown editions are read and ignored, so an older Wren keeps working with a newer licence. Each field is at most 256 bytes.
  • signature: base64url (no padding) of the Ed25519 signature over "wren-license-v1\n" followed by the payload's bytes exactly as they appear in the text (nothing to canonicalize; the prefix keeps a signature made for another use from passing as a licence).

White space is ignored and lines starting with # are comments, so a key may be wrapped in an e-mail, and a .wrenlicense file starts with a header of comments:

# Wren licence (Supporter) for Jeanne Dupont
# Order WREN-0001, 2026-10-22. Open this file with Wren, or paste the key in about:wren.
WREN1.eyJwcm9kdWN0Ijoid3JlbiIs…
…

#In Wren

  • Enter a key: about:wren (menu → About Wren, or the command palette) has a text box (Register), a Choose a file… button, and accepts a .wrenlicense file dropped on the window, typed in the address bar, or given on the command line (wren.exe jeanne.wrenlicense). A key that does not check out is refused with the reason and nothing is kept.
  • Stored in license.wrenlicense in the profile folder (browser.license.path points elsewhere; with browser.profile.persist off it lives in memory for the session). It is read and checked only when about:wren is opened.
  • Remove it with Remove the licence from this computer on the same page.
  • Preferences (about:config): browser.license.path, browser.license.public_key (replaces the built-in key, to read licences of another issuer), browser.license.support_url (the Support Wren link, a web page).

#The maintainer's procedure

#1. Make the key pair (once)

PowerShell
tools\license.ps1 keygen

This writes the private key to %USERPROFILE%\.wren-license\private.key (outside the repository: keygen refuses a path inside a git work tree, and .gitignore keeps .wren-license/, private.key and *.wrenlicense out of git) and prints the public key and the line to paste in src/license/public_key.odin:

Odin
PRODUCTION_PUBLIC_KEY :: "…"

Rebuild Wren. Back up the private key outside this computer (a password manager): if it is lost, no new licence can be issued for the builds that carry the public key, and if it leaks, anyone can issue licences. keygen will not overwrite an existing key without -force; a new key invalidates every licence issued with the old one.

Until the public key is set, builds read no licence: about:wren stays on Unregistered, and pasting a key says that this build has no key to check it with.

#2. Issue a licence

PowerShell
tools\license.ps1 issue -name "Jeanne Dupont" -email jeanne@example.org -edition supporter -order WREN-0001

-edition is supporter or patron; -date defaults to today; -private FILE uses another key. The tool verifies what it signed, prints the key, and writes %USERPROFILE%\.wren-license\issued\WREN-0001.wrenlicense (-out FILE to choose). Send the file (or the key) to the buyer.

Other commands: tools\license.ps1 pubkey (print the public key), tools\license.ps1 verify FILE (check a licence against the built-in key; -public KEY against another).

#3. Development key

-dev uses a development pair that is public on purpose (src/license/dev_keys.odin: the tests and screenshots use it). A licence made with it is refused by a build that carries the production key. To try one in a build: tools\license.ps1 issue -dev … and --pref browser.license.public_key=<tools\license.ps1 pubkey -dev>.

An experimental build (tools\experimental.ps1, which builds with WREN_ACCEPT_DEV_LICENSE_KEY=1: build.bat passes -define:WREN_ACCEPT_DEV_LICENSE_KEY=true) accepts the licences of this pair too, as a development build does, so that the demonstration licence it is handed out with shows its card with no setting. A release never does.

A pre-registered build carries a licence inside: build.bat with WREN_EMBEDDED_LICENSE=<the one line of the .wrenlicense> (and a WREN_VERSION_LABEL, which it requires so that such a build is never an unlabelled one). The first time about:wren asks the profile for its licence and the profile holds none, the build's is written there (license_seed, src/browser/license_shell.odin) with a marker file <licence file>.seeded; it is then the profile's own: Remove the licence removes it and the marker stops it coming back, another licence replaces it, and a profile that already holds a licence keeps its own. A build that cannot check the text (a release with no key for it) puts nothing anywhere. tools\experimental.ps1 builds this way with the development pair's demonstration licence. A release has no WREN_EMBEDDED_LICENSE.

#4. Without the Worker

tools\license.ps1 issue still works for a gift, a refund replacement or a licence given by hand, with the same key. Use an order number that does not look like a Worker one (GIFT-0001).

#Selling with Paddle

Nothing is for sale until the steps below are done: the support page shows Coming soon while its settings are empty. Cost: Paddle's fee per sale, the free plans of Cloudflare Workers + KV, and, to mail licences to buyers you do not know, the Workers Paid plan (5 USD a month, 3000 mails a month included, then 0.35 USD per 1000: see "Mailing the licence" below).

buyer ── Paddle checkout (overlay on support.html) ── pays
                │                                       │
                │ checkout.completed (browser)          │ transaction.completed (signed webhook)
                ▼                                       ▼
        thanks.html?txn=txn_…                    Worker POST /paddle/webhook  verifies Paddle-Signature,
                │                                        │                     then hands the transaction to
                │ GET /licence?txn=txn_…                 ▼                     the LicenseOrder Durable Object
                │                                 LicenseOrder(txn)  ── reads the customer (Paddle API), signs,
                └──────────────► Worker ◄── KV ◄──  (one per purchase)   writes the KV copy, mails it (Email Service);
                     shows the key, the .wrenlicense       │             a failed mail waits on the object's alarm
                     download (from the KV copy)           └── retry queue: 1, 5, 30 min … then dead-letter

The Durable Object is what makes a double webhook safe: Cloudflare runs at most one instance of a given object at a time and serialises calls to it, so two deliveries of the same transaction.completed, even at the very same instant, are handled one after the other. KV is no longer the authority (its reads and writes are not a transaction); it is the globally-replicated copy the thank-you page reads, kept in step by the object.

#What the Worker does

Endpoint
POST /paddle/webhookChecks Paddle-Signature (ts=…;h1=…: HMAC-SHA256 of ts: + the raw body with the destination's secret, compared in constant time, ts within WEBHOOK_TOLERANCE_SECONDS, 300 by default; several h1 are accepted during a secret rotation). Only transaction.completed acts. The transaction is handed to its LicenseOrder Durable Object: edition from the price ids, name and e-mail from the Paddle API (GET /customers/{id}), licence signed, stored under txn:<id>, mailed (or queued). Answers 200 when done or queued, 401 for a bad signature, 422 for a transaction that can never work (no customer e-mail: nothing to retry), 500 when the Paddle API is down (Paddle then delivers the webhook again). A mail that cannot go out now no longer makes the webhook fail: the object queues it and retries on its own alarm. A transaction with no Wren price is acknowledged and ignored.
POST /mail/bounceThe mail provider's delivery webhook (a bounce or complaint). Protected by MAIL_BOUNCE_SECRET (the X-Bounce-Secret header or a bearer token), closed when that is unset. Body {"txn"|"order": …, "reason": …}: marks that purchase's mail failed and dead-letters it. Cloudflare Email Service has no such webhook today, so this is deliberately provider-agnostic (use it by hand, or wire a provider that has one).
GET /licence?txn=txn_…For thanks.html. 200 with the licence, 202 (Retry-After: 3) while the webhook has not been processed.
GET /licence/txn_….wrenlicenseThe file, as a download.
POST /resend {"email": "…"}Mails the licences bought with that address again ("resend" as in "send again"; the settings keep that name). Off unless RESEND_ENABLED is true (and the ADMIN_TOKEN bearer when RESEND_REQUIRE_TOKEN). Same answer whether or not the address bought something; at most RESEND_MAX_PER_HOUR (3) mails per address and hour. Every mail goes back through the order's object (never sent straight from here). It ignores the mail state of the purchase, so it is also the way to get a licence whose first mail failed, was lost, or dead-lettered.
GET /admin/dead-letterThe mails that gave up (Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN). An order, a code, a count, a time: no name, no address. POST /admin/dead-letter/retry {"txn":"txn_…"} re-queues one.
GET /health{"ok": true}, or 503 with the names of the settings not set yet (ORDERS is one).

Properties worth knowing:

  • Idempotent, atomically. The licence is a function of the transaction (Ed25519 signatures are deterministic, the date is the transaction's own, the order number is derived from its id: txn_01hv8wptq8987qeep44cyrewp9 gives WREN-EEP4-4CYR-EWP9). The LicenseOrder Durable Object serialises every delivery of the same webhook, so two of them, even at the same instant, issue one licence and send one mail — the race KV alone could not close. order:<number> in KV finds the transaction of an order number.

  • One mail per purchase, at least once and never twice. Email Service has no idempotency key (a second send() is a second mail), so the object's state decides, under its input gate. mail goes pending → sending → sent (or failed/dead/skipped). sending is written to the object's own storage before send() is called: if the object is cut off mid-send, a later wake reads sending and does not send again (the attempt may have gone out and cannot be confirmed), so the buyer, who got nothing, asks with POST /resend, which forces one more attempt.

    • The retry queue is the object's alarm, not Paddle's redelivery. An error that means "nothing was sent" (E_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, E_DAILY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, E_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR) puts the mail back to pending and schedules the next attempt on a backoff ladder (MAIL_BACKOFF_MINUTES, default 1, 5, 30, 120, 720, 2880 minutes; the last rung repeats). The webhook is acknowledged (200) either way: the object owns the retry now.
    • Dead-letter. After MAIL_MAX_ATTEMPTS tries (default 7) that all deserved a retry, the mail is dead and a small record lands under dead:<txn> (order, code, count, time — no personal data), listed by GET /admin/dead-letter. Re-queue it with POST /admin/dead-letter/retry or /resend once the provider is well.
    • A bounce reported to POST /mail/bounce marks the mail failed and dead-letters it (alert and consult).
    • Every other error (E_SENDER_NOT_VERIFIED, E_RECIPIENT_NOT_ALLOWED, E_DELIVERY_FAILED, a bad address, …) is final right away: failed, with the code in mail_detail.
  • The id is the only secret of GET /licence. It is a ULID (80 random bits): not guessable, known to the buyer and to Paddle. What it yields is a licence that unlocks nothing. Responses carry Cache-Control: no-store, and CORS is limited to ALLOWED_ORIGIN.
  • The key never leaves unchecked. The Worker verifies each signature against LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY before using it, and refuses to start signing when the private key and the public key are not a pair.
  • Names are made safe to sign: control and bidi characters become spaces, 256 bytes at most (what Wren accepts). A customer without a name gets their e-mail address as name.
  • Logs hold event names, transaction ids, order numbers, statuses and Email Service error codes: never a name, an address, a key or a secret (the message of an Email Service error can quote the address, so it is not logged).
  • KV writes: four per purchase (txn: when the mail starts, order:, email:, txn: again when it settles; one more per retry or bounce). Nothing else writes, except /resend for an address that really bought (so a flood of made-up addresses uses none).
  • Retention (RGPD). KV keeps the buyer's name and e-mail address next to the licence (that is how the page shows it and how /resend mails it again). PII_RETENTION_DAYS days after the mail settles, the object purges them: the record's name, email, licence and file are blanked (name becomes (purged)), the email: index is dropped; what stays is the order number and a note that it was purged. The licence is reproducible from the public transaction id, so nothing is really lost; the person is. Set PII_RETENTION_DAYS=0 to keep forever. Delete one by hand before then: npx wrangler kv key delete --binding LICENSES --remote "txn:txn_…" (and order:…; the email: index only holds a hash).

#The order object: state and failure scenarios

Each LicenseOrder keeps, in its own SQLite-backed storage (durable, transactional with its input gate):

OrderState {
  status: "received" | "issued" | "mailed" | "failed",
  stored: { … the signed licence, the buyer, the mail state and attempts … } | undefined,
  attempts: number,              // send() calls made
  next_attempt: ISO string | undefined,   // when the retry alarm will fire
  journal: [ { at, evt, detail? } ]        // the last ~40 steps, no personal data
}

The mail state (stored.mail) is the one KV mirrors: pending (owed, maybe queued), sending (a send is in flight, its outcome unknown), sent, failed (final defeat), dead (gave up after the attempt cap while every try deserved a retry), skipped (no sender configured yet). The single alarm serves two non-overlapping phases: the retry queue while a mail is owed, then the RGPD purge once it is settled.

What happens when things go wrong:

  • A webhook delivered twice (Paddle retries on any non-2xx; it can also fire two near-simultaneous deliveries). Both reach the same object; its input gate runs them one after the other. The first issues and mails; the second finds issued/mailed and returns replayed without signing or sending again.
  • The mail provider is down (a rate/daily limit, a 5xx). The object marks pending, sets its alarm for the next backoff rung, and acknowledges the webhook (200). The alarm retries — 1, 5, 30, 120, 720, 2880 minutes — until it succeeds or reaches MAIL_MAX_ATTEMPTS, then dead-letters. Paddle is not involved in the retry.
  • The object is cut off mid-send (a redeploy, a timeout, an eviction). sending was written before send(), so the next wake does not send again (the mail may have gone, and we cannot confirm it). The buyer uses /resend, or you re-queue from the dead-letter; /resend forces one more attempt whatever the state.
  • The Worker is redeployed in the middle. A new code version keeps talking to the same objects (same ids, same storage); the v1 migration already ran, so the class is unchanged. In flight requests finish or are retried by Paddle; the object's state is the source of truth, so nothing is issued or mailed twice.
  • The object's storage is lost (a reset, or an old KV-only record from before this change). On the next call the object rehydrates stored from the KV copy by its transaction id, so /resend and reads still work; it is authoritative again from there.
  • The Paddle API is down while reading the customer. The object throws, the webhook answers 500, nothing is stored, and Paddle delivers again later. No half-issued state is left behind.

#1. Accounts

  • Cloudflare (free): cf auth login (the CLI is cf, a pnpm package: pnpm add -g cf).
  • Paddle: a sandbox account first (https://sandbox-vendors.paddle.com: separate from the live one, no verification, no money), the live account later.

#Mailing the licence (Cloudflare Email Service)

The licence is mailed with Cloudflare's own sender (Email Service > Email Sending, in beta), through a send_email binding named EMAIL: no other provider, no API key, no secret to keep. What it needs (the pages of https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/ are the reference and change; read Domain configuration, Send bindings and Pricing before the first deploy):

  1. A domain on Cloudflare DNS that you will send from (the one of MAIL_FROM, for example froment.software).
  2. Onboard it: dashboard > Compute > Email Service > Email Sending > Onboard Domain, choose the domain. Cloudflare adds the DNS records itself (SPF, DKIM and MX on cf-bounce.<domain>, DMARC on _dmarc.<domain>). They usually propagate in 5 to 15 minutes. Without this the sender is refused (E_SENDER_NOT_VERIFIED, E_SENDER_DOMAIN_NOT_AVAILABLE).
  3. The Workers Paid plan. On the free plan the binding only sends to verified destination addresses of your account, so a buyer you do not know gets nothing (E_RECIPIENT_NOT_ALLOWED: the licence stays on the thank-you page). On Workers Paid, any recipient: 3000 mails a month included per account, then 0.35 USD per 1000. At a few sales a month it is the plan's own price (5 USD a month) and nothing more. Sends to your own verified addresses are free, which is enough for a test on the free plan.
  4. MAIL_FROM in cloudflare.config.ts and wrangler.jsonc: an address of the onboarded domain, for example Wren <licences@froment.software> (MAIL_REPLY_TO is optional, for example contact@froment.software: where a buyer's reply goes).
  5. Deploy. The binding is declared in both config files (EMAIL: bindings.sendEmail({}), "send_email": [{"name": "EMAIL"}]) and cf deploy lists it. With MAIL_FROM empty, or when the binding is missing (a local test), the mail is skipped: the Worker still issues the licence and the thank-you page shows it.
  6. Try it: a sandbox purchase (below) with your own e-mail address; Email Sending > Activity log shows the message, and npx wrangler tail shows mail (state: sent) or mail_refused with the error code.

Errors worth knowing (code in the logs, and mail_detail in the record of the purchase): E_SENDER_NOT_VERIFIED, E_SENDER_DOMAIN_NOT_AVAILABLE (onboard the domain, or fix MAIL_FROM), E_RECIPIENT_NOT_ALLOWED (free plan), E_ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED (reputation), E_DELIVERY_FAILED (the buyer's server refused): final, mail: failed. E_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, E_DAILY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, E_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR: the webhook answers 500 and Paddle delivers it again. wrangler dev only logs the mail (add "remote": true to the binding to send for real, to a test address).

#2. Keys

PowerShell
tools\license.ps1 keygen     # once; see "Make the key pair". Public key -> src/license/public_key.odin, rebuild Wren
tools\license.ps1 pubkey     # prints it again (LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY)

LICENSE_PRIVATE_KEY is the line of %USERPROFILE%\.wren-license\private.key that is not a # comment.

#3. Deploy the Worker (sandbox first)

The Worker needs Paddle's webhook secret, which Paddle only gives once the Worker has an address. So: deploy, create the destination in Paddle, then put the secrets in.

PowerShell
cd licence\worker
pnpm install                                   # cf and wrangler, dev dependencies used to build and deploy
cf auth login
copy secrets.example.env secrets.sandbox.env   # fill LICENSE_PRIVATE_KEY now; the others after step 4

Edit the settings and env in cloudflare.config.ts (it is what cf reads; wrangler.jsonc is the same thing for npx wrangler, keep the two alike): LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY, MAIL_FROM, MAIL_REPLY_TO if you want one. Then:

PowerShell
cf deploy --mode sandbox --secrets-file secrets.sandbox.env

--mode sandbox is a second Worker, wren-licence-sandbox, with its own KV namespace (created by the first deploy), so the sandbox and the live shop never mix. The command prints the address, https://wren-licence-sandbox.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev. Check it: https://…/health lists what is still missing.

Durable Objects need the Workers Paid plan. The Worker uses one LicenseOrder object per purchase; the first deploy runs the v1 migration that creates its SQLite-backed class (declared in both config files: migrations with new_sqlite_classes in wrangler.jsonc, newSqliteClasses in cloudflare.config.ts). On the free plan the deploy is refused. Since mailing a stranger already needs Workers Paid (below), the shop needs the paid plan to run for real anyway; a free-plan deploy can still issue licences to the thank-you page if you drop the Durable Object, but then the double-webhook and the retry queue are gone. Later migrations get a new tag and are appended, never edited.

cf deploy --dry-run --mode sandbox builds and shows the bindings without uploading. To change one secret later: cf workers secrets update PADDLE_API_KEY --worker wren-licence-sandbox --text …, or edit the file and deploy again. To create the namespace yourself: cf kv namespaces create --title wren-licences-sandbox, then LICENSES: bindings.kv({ id: "…" }).

Same with Wrangler (what cf runs underneath; use it if cf lacks a command):

PowerShell
npx wrangler deploy --env sandbox                       # production: npx wrangler deploy
npx wrangler secret bulk secrets.sandbox.json --env sandbox    # {"LICENSE_PRIVATE_KEY": "...", ...}
npx wrangler tail --env sandbox                         # live logs

#4. Paddle sandbox

  1. Catalog → Products → New product: "Wren licence" (category: standard digital goods). Add two one-time prices (no billing period): Supporter 29 EUR and Patron 79 EUR, tax mode "inclusive" so that the buyer pays the displayed price, quantity 1 to 1. Copy both price ids (pri_…).
  2. Developer tools → Notifications → New destination: type Webhook, URL https://wren-licence-sandbox.<subdomain>.workers.dev/paddle/webhook, only the event transaction.completed, active. Open the destination and copy its Secret key (pdl_ntfset_…).
  3. Developer tools → Authentication → API keys → New: server side, with the permission customer: read only. This is PADDLE_API_KEY. Under Client-side tokens → New, create the token for Paddle.js (test_… in the sandbox).

  4. Put the secret, the API key and the prices where they belong:

    • secrets.sandbox.env: PADDLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, PADDLE_API_KEY;
    • cloudflare.config.ts (and wrangler.jsonc): PRICE_SUPPORTER, PRICE_PATRON (several ids may be separated by commas);
    • then cf deploy --mode sandbox --secrets-file secrets.sandbox.env again, and check /health.
  5. Checkout → Checkout settings: Default payment link = https://sachahjkl.github.io/wren/support.html.
  6. The site (site/support.html, the <div id="buy">): data-environment="sandbox", data-client-token, data-price-supporter, data-price-patron, data-worker (the Worker's address, no trailing slash), and in site/thanks.html <main data-worker="…"> the same address. Publish site/ (GitHub Pages), or serve the folder locally for the test (python -m http.server 8765 --directory site: http://localhost:8765/support.html, which the sandbox Worker lets call it).

  7. Try it: press Supporter, pay with the test card 4242 4242 4242 4242, any future expiry, CVC 100. The browser goes to thanks.html?txn=txn_… and shows the key; the e-mail arrives with the file. Check the key:

    PowerShell
    tools\license.ps1 verify -text "WREN1.…" -public <the public key>

    and paste it in about:wren. If something is missing: Developer tools → Notifications → the destination → Logs shows what Paddle sent and got back (a Replay button redelivers it), and npx wrangler tail --env sandbox shows the Worker's side (webhook_rejected with the reason, issued, mail…).

  8. Try the failure paths once if you like: a wrong PADDLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET gives 401 and nothing is stored; a wrong MAIL_FROM (a domain that is not onboarded in Email Sending) records mail: failed with mail_detail: E_SENDER_NOT_VERIFIED (see mail_refused in the logs) while the thank-you page still shows the key.

#5. Production

Same, in the live Paddle account (its own products, prices, ids, destination, secret, API key and client token: the sandbox ones do not exist there). Paddle asks to verify the business and to approve the website domain (Checkout → Website approval: sachahjkl.github.io, or the domain you use). Then:

PowerShell
copy secrets.example.env secrets.env      # live webhook secret, live API key, the private key
# cloudflare.config.ts / wrangler.jsonc: PRICE_* (live ids), LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY, MAIL_FROM (domain onboarded in Email Sending, Workers Paid)
cf deploy --secrets-file secrets.env

Create the live destination with https://wren-licence.<subdomain>.workers.dev/paddle/webhook, and in support.html set data-environment="production", the live data-client-token (live_…), the live price ids and data-worker; in thanks.html the same data-worker. A custom domain for the Worker (for example licences.froment.software) is a triggers.fetch in cloudflare.config.ts (routes in wrangler.jsonc) once the zone is on Cloudflare.

Make a real purchase of your own (and refund it from Paddle) before announcing anything.

#Settings reference

Set in cloudflare.config.ts / wrangler.jsonc (vars), not secret:

Name
PADDLE_API_BASEhttps://sandbox-api.paddle.com or https://api.paddle.com: must match the webhook's environment
PRICE_SUPPORTER, PRICE_PATRONprice ids, comma separated; the patron price wins when both are bought
LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEYthe public key of src/license/public_key.odin
MAIL_FROM, MAIL_REPLY_TOsender (Name <address> or an address, on a domain onboarded in Email Service > Email Sending; empty: no mail) and optional reply address
ALLOWED_ORIGINorigins that may call GET /licence from a page, comma separated (* = any)
WEBHOOK_TOLERANCE_SECONDShow old a webhook may be (300)
RESEND_ENABLED, RESEND_MAX_PER_HOURPOST /resend ("send the licence again") on/off (false) and its limit per address (3)
RESEND_REQUIRE_TOKENtrue also requires the ADMIN_TOKEN bearer on /resend (false)
MAIL_BACKOFF_MINUTESthe mail retry ladder, minutes between attempts, comma separated (1,5,30,120,720,2880); the last rung repeats
MAIL_MAX_ATTEMPTSsend tries before a mail goes to the dead-letter (7)
PII_RETENTION_DAYSdays the buyer's name and address are kept after the mail settles, then purged (90; 0 = never)

Bindings: LICENSES (KV), ORDERS (the LicenseOrder Durable Object namespace), EMAIL (Email Service sending; absent: licences are not mailed, the thank-you page still shows them).

Secrets (secrets.env, uploaded by cf deploy --secrets-file, never in a committed file): LICENSE_PRIVATE_KEY, PADDLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, PADDLE_API_KEY, and optionally ADMIN_TOKEN (for /admin/* and, with RESEND_REQUIRE_TOKEN, /resend) and MAIL_BOUNCE_SECRET (for /mail/bounce). The mail itself needs no secret.

#Tests

PowerShell
cd licence\worker
node --test "test/*.test.ts"      # Node 22.18+ (or: bun test test/); no network, no dependency

tools\test_all.ps1 runs them (SKIP when neither node nor bun is installed). The tests drive the Durable Object through a fake ORDERS namespace (one in-memory LicenseOrder per id, with a fake storage and a manually-fired alarm). They cover the webhook signature (valid, altered, wrong secret, too old, malformed, rotation), a transaction.completed in Paddle Billing's format (licence/worker/test/fixtures), idempotency (a double webhook issues and mails once), the mail outcomes (a fake EMAIL binding: sent, skipped, a deferred mail that the retry alarm later sends, failed, the attachment, no second mail), the endpoints, /resend, and the cross-check: licences made by the Worker with the development pair (DEV_SEED of src/license/dev_keys.odin, read from the Odin source) are verified by Wren's own tool (license.exe verify -dev) as a key and as a .wrenlicense file; altered ones and ones of another key are refused; and for the same fields the Worker and license.exe issue -dev produce the very same text.

#Losing or changing the key

A new key pair invalidates every licence issued with the old one (Wren builds carry one public key). Keep the private key backed up outside this computer; if it leaks, anyone can issue licences, and the only remedy is a new pair, a new Wren build, and a re-issue to every buyer (order: and txn: in KV list them).
